newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sweetens global price to place $3.0 bln.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sweetens global price to place $3.0 bln.

text.p: Brazil priced its 30-year global bond a bit cheaper than market expectations to ensure the size of the deal would hit at least $3.0 billion, Brazilian debt traders said.

The bond, which was offered in exchange for Brady bonds or for outright purchase, has a coupon of 10.125 percent and was priced at 93.234 to yield 10.896 percent, or 395 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries.

"The market was expecting 385 (bps over Treasuries) so I guess it shows it wasn't such a strong deal because they had to price it at 395 to place $3.0 billion," said a Brady trader at a leading Brazilian investment bank.
"I think the (Central Bank) wanted to place more, but $3.0 billion is acceptable. That is what the market expected," the trader said.

After the 1300 GMT/0900 EDT launch, the bond immediately tightened to 370 bps over, and is now at 375 bps, traders said. The global was expected to hold in the 370 to 380 bp over level today, players said.
Mexico did a similar Brady swap last year for a 30-year global bond. The Mexican bond traded today at about 330 bps over Treasuries, traders said.
